transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-10-20 15:00 PT
Duration: 72 minutes
Attendees: Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Head of Platform, GreenWave), Sofia (ML Engineer), Derek (Security), Jamal (SRE), Amira (Product)

--- Summary / Intent (auto):
Quick scoping to capture workload signature for a POC: average QPS, peak bursts, concurrency, token length distributions, and define benchmark pass/fail. Agree on 4-week cadence and deliverables.

[00:00] Morgan (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, um we're gonna run through how we like to profile workloads for POCs — should be practical, open to questions. can you hear me ok?
[00:06] Liam (GreenWave): yep loud and clear. thanks Morgan.
[00:09] Priya (Redwood SE): hi all, i'll focus on the benchmarking harness and what data we need from you to reproduce traffic shapes.
[00:15] Amira (GreenWave Product): quick context — GreenWave runs an e‑commerce conversational assistant inside checkout and a product search re-ranker. both are low-latency but very different token profiles.
[00:24] Sofia (GreenWave ML): right, assistant calls are short prompts (20–60 in) and longer completions (120–400 out). re-ranker is small input (~300 tokens from docs) but expects single token-ish outputs (scores).
[00:36] Priya: good, that helps. two distinct workloads — conversational for latency-sensitive, and re-ranking for throughput. we'll need sample histograms for both. do you have 24–72h of request logs?
[00:45] Sofia: we prepared a 72 hour sample, it's redacted but retains timing. i'll upload it. has a mix of peak shopping hours and overnight low troughs.
[00:55] Morgan: perfect. quick question on SLOs — what are you targeting for p95 and p99 for the conversational assistant?
[01:02] Liam: p95 ideally under 150ms for short 1–2 shot prompts, p99 under 600ms. if we can't hit that on hosted we might consider a private dedicated pool.
[01:12] Derek (Security): and for any private deployment we need KMS integration, audit logs, and SSO via SAML. also data retention policy — logs kept 90 days max.
[01:22] Morgan: noted, we have KMS options and exportable audit logs. we'll attach our SOC2 summary and a network diagram.
[01:28] Jamal (SRE): network wise we prefer VPC peering to avoid public egress, is that supported?
[01:33] Priya: yes, we do VPC peering for Private deployments; hosted can be tunneled but peering is better for consistent latency. expect firewall ports for TLS and the peering CIDR.
[01:42] Amira: timeline question — what's realistic for the POC?
[01:45] Morgan: our typical is 3–4 weeks: week 0 prep and data transfer, week 1 baseline replay and telemetry, week 2 tuning and model variant runs, week 3 final report and handoff. can stretch if you need deeper infra testing.
[01:58] Sofia: that works. we have a black Friday-like sale in three weeks — want this done before that if possible.
[02:05] Morgan: we can aim to complete bench and handoff by 11/12 if we start next week.
[02:09] Priya: now about metrics we'll capture: throughput QPS aggregated, concurrency (simultaneous open connections), tokens in/out distributions, latency quantiles (p50/p90/p95/p99), GPU util and memory, and cost per 1M tokens for the recommended config.
[02:24] Liam: can you also log cold-starts and KV cache hit rates? our assistant uses cache for session state.
[02:30] Priya: yes we instrument KV cache hits. cold-starts we'll simulate by replaying sessions after idle windows.
[02:36] Jamal: our load pattern has diurnal peaks and 3–5 minute micro-bursts during checkout flows — peaks from 15 QPS baseline to 280 QPS bursts across a 12s window. average concurrency during peak is ~42, but spikes to 120 for several seconds.
[02:52] Morgan: ok that's a very spiky profile — will need burst capacity and autoscaling policies. for Dedicated pools we can reserve baseline and allow burstable capacity; for Hosted we can route to a regional pool with fallback.
[03:05] Amira: important: cost sensitivity. we want to balance latency vs cost. what cost levers do you typically recommend?
[03:12] Priya: batching config, quantized model variants, and prefix caching. for re-ranker we can use higher batch sizes and int8 quantization; for conv assistant we lean on micro-batching and KV cache to keep latency low.
[03:25] Sofia: sample token stats from our 72h file — conversational median input 28 tokens, median output 165 tokens, 90th perc output ~340 tokens. re-ranker input median 320 tokens, outputs are ~6 tokens. token mix will affect throughput and cost a lot.
[03:41] Priya: great — that distribution tells us which kernel paths will be hot and where to expect memory pressure from KV cache.
[03:48] Liam: for acceptance criteria — besides latency, we want throughput capacity: sustain 120 QPS with p95 < 200ms on the conversational workload and handle bursts to 280 QPS with p99 < 700ms and no errors. re-ranker should sustain 600 QPS with 99.9% success and p95 latency under 300ms.
[04:07] Morgan: good, those are concrete. we'll include pass/fail gating in the report and a recommended deployment (hosted vs dedicated) with cost delta.
[04:14] Derek: security gating: SOC2 and encryption at rest/in transit, KMS, SAML SSO, and the option for on-prem air-gapped — can you support an on-prem package?
[04:24] Priya: yes we have a private deployment package that can be installed in air-gapped environments; it requires an extended ops window and there's a one-time license fee. we'll add that as an option.
[04:34] Jamal: for the replay harness — we prefer it run from our infra to avoid egress costs, can you provide a Dockerized harness we run?
[04:40] Priya: absolutely — we'll deliver a replay container and a step-by-step runbook. we'll also provide a script to convert your logs into the replay format.
[04:47] Amira: who owns the benchmark script updates if we need to tweak sessions?
[04:50] Morgan: Redwood will own the initial harness; GreenWave can fork and modify. changes should be versioned in the shared repo.
[04:56] Sofia: we may need token redaction for PII. can the harness redact on the fly?
[05:00] Priya: yes, the converter supports pattern-based redaction. please provide the regex rules.
[05:07] Morgan: ok next steps recap — Priya sends harness and runbook, Morgan sends SOC2 doc and network diagram, Sofia uploads 72h sample, Jamal provides peering/firewall, and we'll schedule infra Q&A next week.
[05:20] Liam: one last technical — do you support automatic fallback to smaller model variants if the primary is overloaded?
[05:26] Priya: yes, smart routing with fallback to compatible quantized variants is supported. we can include that in the baseline run.
[05:33] Amira: can we see cost delta estimates up front? ballpark is fine for decision making.
[05:37] Morgan: we'll provide cost per 1M tokens for the recommended configs and an estimate for Dedicated reserved baseline vs pay-as-you-go hosted.
[05:46] Derek: SLA question — do you provide uptime SLAs for Dedicated?
[05:50] Morgan: yes, Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. details in the enterprise addendum. we'll attach the SLA doc.
[05:57] Priya: i'll list the exact telemetry we'll collect in the benchmark template: qps by minute, concurrency time-series, token histograms, GPU util, latency quantiles, error rates, cache hit ratio, memory pressure.
[06:10] Jamal: if we run the replay from our infra, what's the minimal credential set we need to hand out?
[06:15] Morgan: we'll do short-lived API keys for the test, and if peering is used, credentials for the peered endpoint only. no long-term keys.
[06:22] Sofia: about model versions — we might want to test two: the current 13B fine-tuned + a 7B quantized to see cost/latency tradeoffs. are both supported?
[06:31] Priya: yes we can host both and measure. quantized 7B should give big cost wins and lower latency for short responses, but will be assessed for quality.
[06:39] Morgan: ok i'm going to do a quick recap of milestones and responsibilities. week 0 (this week): data handoff and security docs. week 1: baseline replay on hosted + telemetry. week 2: variant runs and tuning (quantization, batching). week 3: stress bursts and autoscaling tests, week 4: final report and decision meeting.
[06:59] Liam: sounds good. can we compress to 3 weeks?
[07:02] Morgan: maybe if we parallelize baseline and security review — but we should leave some room for unexpected infra tweaks. we'll try for 3.5 weeks.
[07:10] Amira: ok thanks everyone. any last questions?
[07:13] Derek: none from security. thanks.
[07:15] Morgan: thanks all — we'll circulate the artifacts and schedule the infra Q&A. talk soon.
